cards.text: Here's a Psalm of David, written for the choirmaster and set according to Jeduthun, one of the musicians chosen to give thanks to the LORD (1 Chronicles 16:41). This one's a song, friend. David starts by telling us where his soul goes to rest.

cards.question: David says his soul finds rest in God and in his own strength.

cards.text: Then he stacks up the pictures. God alone is his rock, his salvation, his fortress. David's piling SAFE on top of SAFE like I stack cookie boxes when somebody's watching.

cards.question: With God as his rock and his fortress, what does David say about himself?

answers.text: He will never lose a battle

cards.text: Then David speaks to the people threatening a man: "How long will you threaten a man?" I bet this has been going on a while.

cards.question: David asks if they'll all throw that man down. He pictures the man as something already tipping over. What is it?

cards.text: Their whole plan is to cast him down from his lofty perch. And they delight in lies.

cards.question: These people are two-faced. With their mouths they ___, but inwardly they ___.

cards.text: Blessing out loud, cursing inside. That's a "your call is important to us" recording, friend: lovely words, and NOBODY'S picking up. Then comes a Selah, and David turns to talk to his own soul: "Rest in God alone, O my soul."

cards.question: David tells his soul to rest in God alone because his hope comes from Him.

cards.text: Then that line comes back: God alone is his rock, his salvation and his fortress, and David will not be shaken. And now his salvation and his honor rest on God, his strong rock.

cards.question: Now David turns to everybody listening, "O people" and he tells them to trust God at ___ times.
David tells the people to keep their hearts to themselves and stay quiet before God.

cards.text: Then he says it plain: "God is our refuge." And next, David sizes people up: "Lowborn men are but a vapor; the exalted are but a lie."

cards.question: Weighed on a scale, what happens to these men, lowborn and exalted alike?

cards.text: Pile ALL of them on that scale together and it still reads like nobody's standing on it. Then David gives a warning: "Place no trust in extortion or false hope in stolen goods."

cards.question: David says that if your riches increase, you should set your heart upon them.

cards.text: Then David says God has spoken once, and he has heard it twice. ONCE! Friend, my oven timer has to ding NINE times before I hear it one time.

cards.question: God has spoken once, and David heard it twice. What did David hear?
Power belongs to God, and loving devotion belongs to the Lord too. Then David ends with this: God will ___ each man according to his ___.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "Rest in God alone, O my soul.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Then he stacks up the pictures.' 'God alone is his rock, his salvation, his fortress.' 'David's piling SAFE on top of SAFE like I stack cookie boxes when somebody's watching.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke's action doesn't match the fact. David piles up pictures of safety (rock, salvation, fortress). Stacking cookie boxes 'when somebody's watching' is about showing off for an audience, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question says the man is pictured as 'something already tipping over.' That rules out both wrong answers, a tall cedar and a city gate, because neither is tipping. Only 'A leaning wall' fits the hint.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Blessing out loud, cursing inside.' 'That's a "your call is important to us" recording...' 'Then comes a Selah, and David turns to talk to his own soul...' It also carries more than two beats: a recap of card 8's answer, the joke, and the Selah turn to v5.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke's action doesn't match the fact. Psalm 62:4 is about blessing with the mouth while cursing inwardly, which is hidden hostility. A 'your call is important to us' recording with nobody picking up is about being ignored, not about secretly cursing someone.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'hard' (trust God at hard times) is something a baker could argue is right, since trusting God at all times includes hard times.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
